top_story.headline: Rep. Anthony Brown's campaign committee reports more than $800,000 in charity donations and says it will wind down
top_story.dek: The Form 99 was filed Wednesday, October 7, answering an FEC letter dated September 2.
paragraphs: Anthony Brown for Congress, the campaign committee of Rep. Anthony Brown (D-MD), told the Federal Election Commission that its October quarterly report disclosed over $800,000 in donations to charities and that the committee "intends to finalize operations in the coming months." The letter, signed by compliance director Allison P. Murray, responds to a September 2 FEC request about the committee's status.

The letter does not say which charities received the money or give the exact total, and it does not explain why a committee tied to a sitting member of Congress is winding down. Federal rules bar converting campaign funds to personal use but allow charitable donations.
The same compliance director signed an October 7 letter for Eric Lynn for Congress saying that committee will stay open while Lynn considers a future run.

sections.headline: Nine committees tied to sitting House members filed today: three Form 99 replies, five RFAIs and one termination approval
paragraphs: Three members answered September 2 FEC letters with Form 99 submissions. The five RFAIs cover contribution-limit, refund, vendor-disclosure and purpose-of-disbursement problems. The FEC candidate database also flags Friends of Elizabeth Esty and Brenda Lawrence for Congress as incumbent committees, but both belong to former members and are listed under Form 99 Correspondence.

items: Rep. Anthony Brown(D-MD) — Form 99 answering a Sept. 2 FEC letter about the committee's status: the committee says its October quarterly report disclosed over $800,000 in donations to charities and that it 'intends to finalize operations in the coming months.' Filing.

Rep. Brian Jack(R-GA-3) — Form 99 replying to a Sept. 2 request for information: the previous treasurer amended the July quarterly report to remove expense checks that were never issued but had been reported, which changed the reported expense total. The committee says it is changing treasurer and compliance consultant. Filing.

Rep. Ted Lieu(D-CA) — Form 99 saying the committee amended its 12-day pre-primary report (04/01–05/13/2026) to add a credit card transaction and the matching card balance as debt, because the statement arrived after the filing deadline. Filing.

Rep. Darrell Issa(R-CA), April quarterly RFAI — FEC says the report shows primary-designated contributions received after the candidate's 3/6/2026 announcement that he would not seek office; those must be refunded unless the committee had net campaign debts when each arrived. Filing.

Rep. Steve Scalise(R-LA-1), July quarterly RFAI — Asked about refunds of contributions on Schedule A that don't match any originally reported contribution, and about earmarked contributions passed through a conduit without the original donors itemized. Filing.

Rep. Troy Carter(D-LA-2), July quarterly RFAI — Asked to itemize the original vendors behind credit card payments on Schedule B (memo entries are required once a vendor passes $200 in the cycle). Filing.

Rep. Adriano Espaillat(D-NY-13), pre-primary RFAI — Asked to explain vague disbursement purposes: 'Administrative Fees,' 'March April Consulting Services,' 'May Consulting Services,' 'Payment' and 'Professional Services.' Filing.

Rep. Ron Estes(R-KS-4), April quarterly RFAI — Asked about contributions that appear to exceed the per-election limit of $3,500 for individuals, with several $3,500 entries cited on an attached list. Filing.
Rep. Haley Stevens(D-MI-11) — Termination approval for her committee (listed from the filing description; the PDF was not read). Filing.

sections.headline: Twenty candidate-committee RFAIs from non-incumbents, mostly about loans, earmarked contributions and contribution limits
paragraphs: Dated October 7, these letters go to challengers, open-seat candidates, one Senate candidate and one joint fundraising committee. Two committees (Ben4Congress and Jennifer Konfrst for Congress) were told their termination reports are not yet sufficient. Shrewsbury for Senate reported a negative cash balance.

items: Kathleen Riebe for Congress(House), July quarterly — FEC says the committee took contributions designated for a '2026 Primary' the candidate won't enter, alongside '2026 Convention' money; those must be refunded or redesignated, and a $15,000 total and 4/10/2026 receipts are cited. Filing.
Shonique Williams for Congress(House), year-end 2025 — Earmarked contributions routed through a conduit were reported without itemizing the original donors. Filing.
Shonique Williams for Congress(House), April quarterly — Beginning cash doesn't match the 2025 year-end ending balance, and earmarked conduit contributions lack donor itemization. Filing.

Abel Chavez for Congress(House), July quarterly — In-kind contributions were wrongly shown as memo entries (which understates receipts and disbursements), and 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions of $1,000 or more may be missing. Filing.
Committee to Elect Monique Appeaning(House), April quarterly — Loan disclosure lacks a due date and interest rate for a $34,871.63 candidate loan dated 2/1/2026. Filing.
Committee to Elect Monique Appeaning(House), July quarterly — Same loan gap, now also covering a $2,427.53 loan dated 4/1/2026. Filing.

Committee to Elect Monique Appeaning(House), pre-primary — Same two loans lack due date and interest rate, and the committee must say whether the candidate loans came from personal funds or borrowed money. Filing.

Claire Valdez for Congress(House), pre-primary — Transfers from 'Avila Chevalier and Valdez Victory Fund' look like joint fundraising proceeds, but that committee isn't listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization. Filing.
Lander for Congress(House), pre-primary — Redesignated or reattributed contributions from 'Connell, Francesca' weren't reported in the required three-entry format. Filing.
Terri DeBoer for Congress(House), pre-primary — Contributions that appear to exceed the per-election limit. Filing.
Gottheimer Horsford Victory Fund 2026(joint fundraising committee), July quarterly — Report rejected as filed; it must be resubmitted on FEC Form 3. Filing.

Bushra for Congress(House), April quarterly — Contributions designated for the 2026 primary arrived after the primary, which is allowed only to the extent the committee had net debts outstanding. Filing.
Self for Congress(House), April quarterly — Schedule B shows refunds of contributions that were never reported as received. Filing.

Shrewsbury for Senate(Senate), July quarterly — Reports a negative ending cash balance of $2,854.25, which suggests an overdraft, a math error or an unreported debt (an overdraft could be a prohibited bank contribution); operating expenses also appear on the wrong summary line. Filing.
Baker for Congress(House), July quarterly — Purposes are missing for itemized expenditures. Filing.

Ben4Congress(House), April quarterly — An amended report shows $242,685.21 more in disbursements than the original; the committee must explain why, supply missing vendor addresses and clarify purposes listed as 'Consulting' and 'Consulting Fees.' Filing.
Ben4Congress(House), termination report — The committee hasn't shown it meets the conditions to terminate (settled debts, plan for residual funds) and must keep filing until FEC approves. Filing.
Jennifer Konfrst for Congress(House), April quarterly — Schedule B shows a contribution to another candidate that appears to exceed the $2,000-per-election limit for authorized committees. Filing.
Jennifer Konfrst for Congress(House), termination report — Corrections to the April quarterly report are required before FEC will approve termination. Filing.
Sydney Gruters for Congress(House), July quarterly — Earmarked conduit contributions were reported without itemizing the original donors. Filing.

sections.eyebrow: Requests for Additional Information — PACs and Party Committees
sections.headline: Twenty-eight PAC and party RFAIs, led by unreported independent expenditures and a union refund question
paragraphs: Most are routine arithmetic or itemization fixes. The ones with substance: Road Sprinkler Fitters Local Union No. 669 PAC's $20,863.51 refund of a deposit "made in error," Vote Rev PAC's reimbursements to an unregistered organization, and MAHA PAC's unitemized and possibly late independent-expenditure reports for Julia Letlow.

items: Electing Ethical Democrats(PAC), July quarterly — Contributions that appear to exceed the limits for contributions to a candidate. Filing.

Lucete Leadership Fund(PAC), July quarterly — Independent expenditures supporting 'Villegas, Randy' on Schedule E ($3,412.83 to 'Communities for A New California' and $11,959.09 to 'RCBS Payroll') don't match Schedule D, which shows -$4,000.00 and -$16,628.42. Filing.
SC Rising(PAC), July quarterly — Independent-expenditure purposes 'MESSAGIG TO SUPPORT' and 'MESSAGING TO OPPOSE' are too vague. Filing.

Vote Rev PAC(PAC), July quarterly — Payments labeled 'Reimbursement of Administrative Expenses' to 'Vote Rev,' an apparently unregistered organization, look like in-kind contributions; FEC asks for dates the goods or services were provided. Filing.

Road Sprinkler Fitters Local Union No. 669 PAC(union PAC), June monthly — $20,863.51 paid back to the union as 'Refund of contribution (deposit made in error)' raises a question about a prohibited union contribution; FEC wants the original deposit date and the receipt reported. Filing.

Western and Southern Life Insurance Co. Political Action Committee(PAC), statement of organization — Line 5(e) says it is a separate segregated fund, but no connected organization is identified. Filing.
MAHA PAC(PAC), September monthly — A 24-hour independent-expenditure report may have been filed late. Filing.
MAHA PAC(PAC), June monthly — Calendar year-to-date totals are wrong, and a 24-hour independent expenditure supporting 'LETLOW, JULIA REP.' was never itemized on Schedule E. Filing.
MAHA PAC(PAC), May monthly — A 48-hour independent expenditure supporting 'LETLOW, JULIA REP.' was never itemized on Schedule E. Filing.

Indivisible Action(PAC), August monthly — Schedule E year-to-date totals look wrong for the Colorado Senate, Minnesota Senate and New York 10th District races, and 24- and 48-hour reports filed with vendors including 'Civitech,' 'Good Influence' and 'Scale to Win' need reconciling. Filing.
North Carolina Democratic Party - Federal(party), August monthly — Schedule H2 allocation ratios for the '2026 Unity Dinner' don't add up to 100%. Filing.
Truth & Accountability Project(PAC), July quarterly — Calendar year-to-date totals on nine summary lines are wrong. Filing.
AB PAC(PAC), August monthly — A 24-hour independent-expenditure report may have been filed late, and 48-hour report items need reconciling. Filing.
Greenberg Traurig, P.A. PAC(PAC), July monthly — An amended report shows $13,120.72 more in receipts than the original; FEC asks why. Filing.
American Academy of Dermatology Association Political Action Committee (SkinPAC)(PAC), August monthly — Contributions that appear to exceed the $5,000 annual limit. Filing.

Boston Scientific Corporation Political Action Committee (BSC PAC)(PAC), August monthly — Donor entries such as 'Boston Scientific / Information Requested' are incomplete; FEC wants the real employer and occupation or proof of best efforts. Filing.

Lennox Employee Advocacy Program Lennox International Inc.(PAC), July quarterly — Beginning cash doesn't match the April quarterly closing balance, year-to-date totals are off, and the January 1 cash figure changed between reports. Filing.
Vanteo, LLC Political Action Committee(PAC), July monthly — An amended report shows $21,000 more in disbursements than the original. Filing.
PictSweet Company Good Government Committee(PAC), July quarterly — Report wasn't signed by the treasurer or agent on file. Filing.
Citizens for the Legalization of Cannabis Political Action Committee(PAC), July quarterly — Report wasn't signed by the treasurer or agent on file. Filing.
Montana Voters PAC(PAC), post-general 2024 — An amended report shows $150,000 more in receipts than the original. Filing.
Bernadette Victory Fund(joint fundraising committee), statement of organization — Asked to clarify its relationship with 'Bernadette for Congress,' listed as a participant, or remove it. Filing.
Project 218(PAC), September monthly — Line 8 cash-on-hand arithmetic is incorrect. Filing.
Congressional Black Caucus PAC(PAC), August monthly — Line 8 cash-on-hand arithmetic is incorrect. Filing.
Old North Leadership PAC(PAC), statement of organization — Asked to clarify its relationship to 'Rouzer Congressional Trust,' which looks like a joint fundraising representative. Filing.
Republican Mainstreet Partnership PAC(PAC), September monthly — Year-to-date totals are wrong on three lines, and some contributions appear to exceed limits. Filing.
Montana Republican State Central Committee(party), September monthly — Year-to-date totals are wrong on four lines. Filing.

Energy Transfer Employee Management Company PAC (Energy Transfer PAC)(PAC), October quarterly — Beginning cash doesn't match the July quarterly closing balance, and year-to-date totals and Line 8 are wrong. Filing.

sections.headline: Twelve Form 99 submissions from other committees, mostly replies to the September 2 residual-funds letters
paragraphs: Several former and non-running candidates told the FEC what will happen to leftover money. Friends of Elizabeth Esty says funds left since 2018 pay storage and winding-down costs. A treasurer's resignation letter for Khalifa for Congress, and a presidential candidate committee's scanned report that appears to show zeros throughout, are also in the batch.

items: Friends of Elizabeth Esty(former Rep., D-CT) — Letter answering FEC questions on the April and July quarterly reports: residual funds from the 2018 election are being kept to pay winding-down costs such as storage, including payments to 'Black's Self-storage' and 'Self-storage of Cheshire,' and the treasurer says no money has been or will be converted to personal use. Filing.

Brenda Lawrence for Congress(former Rep., D-MI) — Treasurer says the committee is working with legal counsel to transfer residual campaign funds to an eligible 501(c)(3) organization, in reply to a Sept. 2 letter. Filing.

Eric Lynn for Congress(House) — Reply to a Sept. 2 letter: Eric Lynn is not a candidate but is keeping the committee open while he considers a future run, and meanwhile will spend funds supporting candidates for federal and local office. Filing.
Alek for Oregon(House) — Says no committee assets were converted to personal use and the residual funds will be disposed of in line with FEC rules; it will keep filing periodic reports. Filing.
Esshaki for Congress(House) — Same wording as Alek for Oregon: no personal use, residual funds to be disposed of later, periodic reports continue. Filing.

Caryn for Congress Inc.(House) — Asked what will happen to residual cash shown on the 3/31 and 6/30 reports; the committee plans to pay wrap-up expenses and repay candidate loans, then file a termination report. Filing.

Khalifa for Congress(House) — Letter from Lisa Croft resigning as treasurer effective September 1, 2026, saying FEC staff told her on September 21 that her name was not listed as treasurer, and asking for the record to be updated. Filing.
Alaine Elizabeth Giuliani(presidential candidate committee) — A scanned Form 3P whose summary page appears to show zeros throughout, filed as a miscellaneous submission. Filing.

BOLD America(PAC) — Reply to a Sept. 2 letter: the August monthly report was amended to correct the payment date to 'Sena Kozar Strategies' on Schedule E, which had differed from the 24-hour report. Filing.
Rural America Rising(PAC) — Says an amended April 2026 report correcting errors was uploaded on October 1 with help from FEC tech support. Filing.

Republican State Committee of Delaware(party) — Responds to three items on the July monthly report: says administrative expenses and salaries were properly disclosed or allocated on Schedule H4, and that it corrected H4 year-to-date totals in a concurrent amended report. Filing.
Wilderness Action, Inc.(PAC) — Filing frequency change notice: switches from quarterly to monthly reports starting with the October monthly report. Filing.

sections.headline: One voided campaign loan from Lily Tang Williams
paragraphs: One large negative transaction appeared in this period. Negative amounts on FEC Schedule A records represent voided, reversed, or refunded transactions—usually routine adjustments, though occasionally the paper trail for something being unwound after the fact.

items: Lily for Congress Committee (ID C00800458): $20,000 voided loan received from the candidate Lily Tang Williams, dated December 31, 2025—listed as "Loans Received from the Candidate" in the FEC record.
